memories.author: D03
memories.text:
85‑year‑old woman presents with chronic insomnia.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports difficulty falling asleep, frequent night awakenings and non‑restorative sleep for the past 6 months, affecting her daytime alertness while driving.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 58 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 24.1 (overweight). Cardiovascular and respiratory exams are normal; no focal neurological deficits.
IMPRESSION: Chronic insomnia, likely exacerbated by age‑related changes. TSH, haemoglobin, fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar are ordered to rule out contributory medical causes.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start melatonin 3 mg at bedtime and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Advise weight‑appropriate diet and regular light activity as BMI ≥23. Return if chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39 °C, or worsening confusion.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Insomnia Severity Index score: 18 (moderate insomnia). I still feel tired in the mornings and sometimes worry about driving while drowsy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up for insomnia after medication change.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports improved sleep onset but still wakes 2‑3 times per night; daytime fatigue less severe.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 59 kg, BMI 24.5 (overweight). No new cardiac or pulmonary findings.
IMPRESSION: Partial response to trazodone 50 mg HS; consider dose adjustment. Labs from April show normal TSH and Hb, fasting glucose mildly high but stable, lipids within target.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase trazodone to 75 mg HS, continue melatonin 3 mg HS. Reinforce diet and activity advice due to BMI ≥23. Return if new palpitations, severe dizziness, falls, or worsening mood.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review of insomnia treatment and side effects.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes morning grogginess and mild dizziness after taking trazodone 75 mg HS; sleep maintenance still imperfect.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 60 kg, BMI 25.0 (obese). No postural hypotension detected.
IMPRESSION: Trazodone likely contributing to daytime sedation; Hb and TSH remain normal. Obesity warrants lifestyle reinforcement.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reduce trazodone to 50 mg HS, keep melatonin 3 mg HS. Advise reduced calorie intake and regular walking as BMI ≥23. Return if fainting, chest pain, shortness of breath, or confusion.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine review of insomnia and cardiovascular risk.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports satisfactory sleep with occasional night awakenings; no daytime sedation.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/78 mmHg, weight 59.5 kg, BMI 24.8 (overweight). Cardiovascular exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia well‑controlled on melatonin 3 mg HS and trazodone 50 mg HS. TSH, haemoglobin, fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar are within target ranges; influenza vaccine offered due to age >60.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current regimen. Give inactivated influenza vaccine today (0.5 mL IM). Reinforce diet and activity advice as BMI ≥23. Return if fever >39 °C, new chest pain, palpitations, or unexplained bleeding.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mid‑year check‑up for insomnia and general health.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient describes occasional early‑morning awakening (≈3 am) but feels rested; no medication side effects.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/76 mmHg, weight 59 kg, BMI 24.5 (overweight). No abnormal findings.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia stable; labs from April show normal thyroid, haemoglobin, lipids and glucose. Continue current sleep regimen.
ARRANGEMENTS: No medication change. Advise maintain weight‑appropriate diet and regular activity as BMI ≥23. Return if new chest pain, severe dyspnoea, fever >39 °C, or sudden confusion.
